title: COVID-19 lockdown effect on retail foot traffic

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
For this analysis, we will use a Difference-in-Differences (DID) approach. This method is appropriate because we want to estimate the causal effect of COVID-19 lockdown orders on retail store foot traffic by comparing the changes in log foot traffic index over time between treated and control groups. The key assumption in a DID analysis is the parallel trends assumption, which presumes that in the absence of treatment, the average change in the outcome variable would have been the same for both treated and control groups.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# Read the data
data_path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s01_data.csv"
data <- read.csv(data_path)

# Convert columns to appropriate types if necessary
data$unit_id <- as.factor(data$unit_id)
data$treated <- as.factor(data$treated)
data$post <- as.factor(data$post)

# Run the DID regression
did_model <- lm(y ~ treated * post, data = data)

# Summarize the model to get the coefficients
summary(did_model)

# Extract the DID estimate and robust standard errors
did_coef <- coef(did_model)["treated1:post1"]
robust_se <- sqrt(diag(vcovHC(did_model, type = "HC1")))

# Print the DID estimate for the interaction term and its robust standard error
cat("DID Estimate (Interaction Term):\n")
cat("Coefficient:", did_coef, "\n")
cat("Robust SE:", robust_se["treated1:post1"], "\n")

# Conduct a basic robustness check: add unit fixed effects
data$unit_id <- as.factor(data$unit_id)  # Ensure unit_id is a factor for fixed effects
did_model_fe <- lm(y ~ treated * post + unit_id, data = data)
summary(did_model_fe)

# Extract the DID estimate from the fixed-effects model
did_coef_fe <- coef(did_model_fe)["treated1:post1"]
robust_se_fe <- sqrt(diag(vcovHC(did_model_fe, type = "HC1")))

# Print the DID estimate for the interaction term and its robust standard error with fixed effects
cat("DID Estimate with Unit FE (Interaction Term):\n")
cat("Coefficient:", did_coef_fe, "\n")
cat("Robust SE:", robust_se_fe["treated1:post1"], "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
We would expect the sign of the "treat_x_post" coefficient to be negative because the strict lockdown likely led to a decrease in foot traffic relative to the locations with minimal restrictions. The magnitude of this effect is anticipated to be substantial given the extensive disruption caused by the COVID-19 lockdowns. Specifically, I expect the coefficient's magnitude to indicate a significant decline in the log foot traffic index, reflecting reduced consumer mobility and activity during the lockdown periods. The robustness checks with unit fixed effects should also reveal consistent results, further confirming the conclusion.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=strict-lockdown counties, control=minimal-restriction counties; shock=March 2020 lockdown
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Strict-lockdown stores show significantly lower foot traffic post-lockdown
_ground_truth.main_effect: ~30% decline in foot traffic for treated stores
